notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Connect the accounting workflow to a trustworthy growth record.
intro: A proposed growth-data workbench for Basis: research the firm’s practice area and operating question, then keep acquisition and lifecycle definitions consistent.
queueIntro: Fictional accounting firms and work-product questions only. No client ledgers, tax returns, audit evidence or accounting advice are included.
workbenchIntro: Prepare an evidence-based commercial brief and data contract. A fit hypothesis does not establish accounting accuracy, compliance or an automated review conclusion.
firstBody: Join firm research, a concrete work-product question and sponsor context to consistent lifecycle states across acquisition and sales systems.

fields.label: Accounting firm and service line mapped
Evaluation timing confirmed or explicitly unknown
Operational sponsor and reviewer roles identified
CRM, marketing and finance lifecycle definitions aligned
Source and influence attribution kept distinct

rules.title: Resolve the firm and practice
rules.next: Distinguish client accounting services, tax, audit and corporate accounting before proposing a workflow.

rules.title: Name the accounting workflow
rules.next: Ask which preparation, reconciliation or review task matters instead of assuming every practice has the same bottleneck.

rules.title: Keep seasonal timing evidence-based
rules.next: Do not infer readiness from the calendar alone. Preserve the source or ask when the team can evaluate a change.

rules.title: Map the implementation and review roles
rules.next: A useful evaluation needs both an operating sponsor and someone who understands the review standard.

rules.title: Repair the lifecycle contract
rules.next: Define lead, qualified opportunity, customer and expansion states before synchronizing systems.

rules.title: Preserve the acquisition evidence
rules.next: Record the original source and later touches separately instead of awarding every channel the same opportunity.

ready.title: Ready for accounting-workflow discovery review
ready.next: The seller can review the practice context, timing and sponsor questions. Product fit and accounting review requirements still need discovery.

experiments.name: Practice-specific discovery
experiments.hypothesis: A relevant accounting work product makes the conversation more useful.
experiments.treatment: CAS, tax or audit workflow question
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Acquisition quality by original source
experiments.hypothesis: Source and influence separation makes channel decisions more reliable.
experiments.treatment: One original source with separately recorded influence
experiments.guardrail: Double counting and incomplete lifecycle joins
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Define the first growth data model
roadmap.body: Agree with Sales and RevOps on firm entities, practice segments, lifecycle states and acquisition attribution.

roadmap.title: Ship one repeatable acquisition motion
roadmap.body: Build research and enrichment for a narrow practice segment. Keep unknowns visible and close the loop with sales.

roadmap.title: Compare growth loops and maintain the stack
roadmap.body: Evaluate outbound and paid cohorts with consistent definitions. Document build-versus-buy decisions and system ownership.
roadmap.measure: Qualified pipeline, acquisition cost and maintenance effort

records.name: Alder Accounting
records.context: A fictional practice is reviewing month-end preparation work.
records.question: Which preparation or reconciliation step creates review rework?

records.name: Cedar Partners
records.context: The firm is classified only as accounting with no service-line detail.
records.question: Which practice would sponsor an evaluation?

records.name: Willow Advisory
records.context: The brief claims a bottleneck without a specific work product.
records.question: What task could the team show in discovery?

records.name: Elm Audit
records.context: Evaluation readiness was inferred solely from a seasonal calendar.
records.question: When can the team actually review a workflow change?

records.name: Birch Accountants
records.context: The operating sponsor is known but the review role is missing.
records.question: Who defines an acceptable review-ready output?

records.name: Juniper Finance
records.context: The same opportunity is counted as sourced by paid search and outbound.
records.question: What was the original source and which touches influenced it?

metricsTitle: Use one lifecycle contract across acquisition and revenue.
metricsIntro: Illustrative definitions expose where a growth system can quietly double count.

rows: Relevant workflow, sponsor and next step
Executed commercial status in source system
Existing customer plus confirmed new scope

metricsNotes: The table proposes a data contract; it is not a description of Basis’s internal systems.
Record first source, later influence and closed revenue separately.
Synthetic accounting examples demonstrate commercial discovery, not accounting advice or client-work automation.
aiApplication: At Basis, I would apply my MCP analytics experience to consistent acquisition and lifecycle definitions, while bounded research agents prepare cited firm and practice context. Reviewer feedback would improve the record before downstream actions are expanded.
